QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_30

question.text: In the context of AIF risk measurement, Standard Deviation primarily measures:

answer.text: Expected return over the risk-free rate
The beta of the portfolio versus a benchmark
Volatility of historical returns from the mean return — a proxy for total historical risk

explanation.text: The Logic: Standard deviation measures the volatility of returns from the mean and is used to ascertain historical risk. The Sharpe ratio uses standard deviation as a measure of total risk, while the Treynor ratio uses beta to capture only systematic risk. The Trap: Option A describes the Sharpe numerator concept. Option B is the beta definition. Option D is wrong because standard deviation captures total risk, not just systematic risk. Note: The standard-deviation definition and its contrast with beta are taken from the risk-measure section of the workbook.
